stem: He said, "It will have been raining since morning."
optA: He said that it would be raining since morning
optB: He said that it have been rained since morning
optC: He said that it would have been raining since morning
optD: He said that it will have been raining since morning
subject: English
solution: In reported speech the future perfect continuous 'will have been raining' shifts back to 'would have been raining'; 'will' becomes 'would' and the rest of the verb group is unchanged. Option (a) drops 'have been' and gives the future continuous instead, (b) is not a grammatical form, and (d) leaves 'will' unchanged, which reported speech does not allow after a past reporting verb.

stem:
It can be inferred from the passage that this year's fire
in Australia is mostly a result of:
optB: An accidental spark in the jungle
optC: A result of an extraordinarily hot and dry spell
optD: A deliberate attempt to put the forests on fire
subject: English
solution: The passage carefully separates the usual causes of bushfires - lightning strikes, an accidental spark, and fires started deliberately - from what made this particular season different. For this year it names the Indian Ocean Dipole, which produced a hot, dry spell across the country, a national temperature record set twice, and a long preceding drought. Lightning and sparks are therefore how fires generally start, not why this season was so much worse than normal. Matches option C.
context:
Since September, at least 25 people have died and thousands have been made homeless. Every state and territory in Australia has experienced fires this summer. But the biggest fires burn along stretches of the eastern and southern coast, where most of the population lives. This includes areas around sydney and Adelaide. More than 6.3 million hectares ( 63,000 sqkm or 15.6 million acres) have been burned so far - one Hectare is roughly the size of a sports field. 

To put that in perspective, around 800,000 Hectares were engulfed in a bush fire in 2018 in California. Australia has always experienced bushfires - it has a "fire season". But this year they are a lot worse than normal. Fires are usually caused by lightning strikes or accidentally by a spark - but some fires are also started deliberately. This year, a natural weather phenomenon known as the 'Indian Ocean Dipole' has meant a hot, dry spell across the country. This year, Australia twice set a new temperature record: an average maximum of 41.9 ∘C was recorded on 18 December. That comes on top of a long period of drought. 

Scientists have long warned that this hotter, drier climate will contribute to fires becoming more frequent and more intense. The more extreme weather patterns and higher temperatures increase the risk of bushfires and allow them to spread faster and wider. Fire fighters are spraying water and fire retardant from planes and helicopters as well as from the ground. But fighting bushfires is extremely difficult and often authorities have to focus on just stopping the Spread, rather than putting the fire out. The spread can for instance be best contained by digging earth boundaries to stop the flames from spreading. The priority is saving lives. Professional fire fighters are the first in line to battle the flames, but they are outnumbered by the thousands of volunteers. Three of them have died. There's also help coming from abroad: the US, Canada and New Zealand have sent firefighters to help. Australia's police, military and navy are involved in rescue and evacuation efforts. While people can flee the fires and are being evacuated, if need be, the flames are devastating wildlife in the affected areas. One study estimated that half a billion animals have died in New South wales alone. Zookeepers take animals home to save them from fire, but the fires don't only kill animals directly, they also destroy the habitat, leaving the survivors vulnerable even when the fires have gone. So, the true scale of loss isn't yet clear. 

Experts say more than 100,000 cows and sheep may also have been lost, which is devastating for farmers. Each state runs its own emergency operation, but Prime Minister Scott Morrison has promised better funding for fire-fighting and payouts for volunteer firefighters, and an additional A$2 billion ( $1. 4billion; £1 billion) for the recovery. But the national government has come under strong criticism from its opponents that it has not been doing enough against climate change. The country is one of the world's biggest per capita greenhouse gas emitters but under international agreements it has committed itself to reduction targets.

S6: It charmed me beyond measure.
P: The buffalo had huge horns.
Q: A kind of unknown calm and peace seemed to slide into my soul.
R: What delighted me most was the sight of a little boy sitting on the last buffalo in the herd.

subject: English

solution: To abate is to become less intense or less widespread, as when a storm or a fever abates. Increase and maintain both go the wrong way, and provoke means to stir something up rather than to reduce it. Matches option B.

stem: CANDID
subject: English
solution: Candid describes speech that is open and truthful even when the truth is unwelcome, so a candid opinion is a frank one. Deceptive is its direct opposite, while careless and dull describe manner or quality rather than honesty. Matches option B.

stem: DILAPIDATED
subject: English
solution: Dilapidated describes a building that has fallen into disrepair through age and neglect, which is what ruined means. Decorated and repaired describe the opposite condition, and expanded is about size rather than state of repair. Matches option C.

stem: ELOQUENT
subject: English
solution: Eloquent describes speech or writing that is fluent, forceful and persuasive, so expressive is the closest match. Silent and awkward are its opposites in fluency, and rigid describes inflexibility rather than the power to express. Matches option C.

stem: FRUGAL
subject: English
solution: Frugal means sparing and careful with money and resources, which is exactly what economical means. Extravagant, wasteful and lavish all name the opposite habit. Matches option C.

stem: HOSTILE
subject: English
solution: Hostile means unfriendly and openly opposed, shading into open aggression. Friendly is its direct opposite, while neutral and calm describe the absence of hostility rather than hostility itself. Matches option C.
context: Choose among the following that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

stem: IMMINENT
subject: English
solution: Imminent describes something about to happen at any moment, so immediate is the closest sense. Distant is its opposite in time and past points the wrong way altogether. Doubtful is the tempting one: it confuses certainty with nearness, but an imminent event is near, not uncertain. Matches option B.
context: Choose among the following that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

stem: LUCID
subject: English
solution: Lucid describes an explanation or piece of writing that is easy to follow, so clear is the meaning. Confusing and vague are its opposites, and dark takes the light metaphor literally instead of reading the sense of the word. Matches option C.
context: Choose among the following that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

stem: OBSOLETE
subject: English
solution: Obsolete describes something no longer in use because it has been superseded, which is what outdated means. Modern, useful and relevant all describe what is still current. Matches option B.
context: Choose among the following that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

stem: PRUDENT
subject: English
solution: Prudent describes someone who acts with care and foresight, so wise is the closest sense. Careless, reckless and rash all name the opposite quality - acting without thought for the consequences. Matches option C.
context: Choose among the following that best expresses the meaning of the given word.

stem: The government decided to ____ the deadline due to public demand.
subject: English
solution: Public demand for more time can only push a deadline further away, so the blank needs a verb meaning to make it longer. Restrict and accelerate would tighten it, and abolish would remove it altogether - none of which is a response to a demand for more time. Matches option A.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: Her calm response helped to ____ the tense situation.
subject: English
solution: The blank must name what a calm response does to tension, which is reduce it. Aggravate, provoke and intensify all make tension worse, so only the remaining verb can fit the sense of the sentence. Worth knowing that the standard spelling for taking the heat out of a situation is 'defuse', from removing a fuse from a bomb; 'diffuse' strictly means to spread something out, and the two are among the most commonly confused pairs in English. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The committee rejected the proposal as it was ____ and impractical.
subject: English
solution: The blank is joined by 'and' to 'impractical', so it must carry a similarly negative sense and give the committee its reason for rejecting the proposal. Viable, realistic and beneficial are all approving words and would leave the sentence contradicting itself. Matches option C.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The teacher asked the students to ____ from using mobile phones in class.
subject: English
subtopic: Contextual Word Selection (Phrasal Verbs and Collocations)
solution: 'Refrain' takes 'from' and means to hold back from doing something, which is what a teacher would ask about phones in class. Indulge and pursue point the opposite way, and insist does not combine with 'from' at all - the preposition sitting after the blank is the real giveaway here. Matches option A.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The actor received widespread ____ for his outstanding performance.
subject: English
solution: An outstanding performance earns praise, and acclaim is precisely enthusiastic public praise. Criticism, condemnation and disregard would all contradict 'outstanding'. Matches option C.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The company suffered huge losses due to ____ planning.
subject: English
solution: Huge losses follow from planning that went wrong, so the blank needs a word carrying that fault. Meticulous, prudent and efficient all describe good planning, and any of them would leave the sentence saying that careful planning caused the losses. Matches option C.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The success of the project largely depends ____ team coordination.
subject: English
solution: 'Depend' takes the preposition 'on' when naming the thing something rests upon. 'Depend in' and 'depend with' are not standard combinations at all, and 'depend for' appears only in the different sense of relying on someone for something, which this sentence does not express. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: He was promoted because of his ____ dedication to work.
subject: English
solution: A promotion rewards dedication that has never faltered, and unwavering means exactly that - steady and unshaken. Casual, reluctant and temporary each weaken the dedication and would remove the very reason given for the promotion. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The doctor advised him to follow a ____ diet.
subject: English
subtopic: Contextual Word Selection (Phrasal Verbs and Collocations)
solution: The fixed collocation a doctor uses is a strict diet - one to be followed without relaxation. Careless and reckless describe the absence of any discipline and cannot be advised. 'Rigid' is the genuinely tempting distractor: it is a real English word with a close meaning, but it normally attaches to rules, structures and attitudes, and it is not the natural partner of 'diet'. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The judge demanded a ____ explanation for the delay.
subject: English
solution: A judge demanding an explanation for a delay wants one that will satisfy the court, and convincing carries exactly that sense. Vague, misleading and partial all describe an explanation a judge would reject, not one a judge would demand. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The organization aims to ____ equal opportunities for all employees.
subject: English
solution: The organisation is working in favour of equal opportunities, so the blank needs a verb of active support. Suppress, deny and evade all work against the stated aim and would make the sentence describe the opposite of an equal-opportunity policy. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

stem: The old bridge was declared ____ for heavy vehicles.
subject: English
solution: A formal declaration about an old bridge and heavy vehicles is a warning, so the blank must carry the negative judgement. Suitable, convenient and accessible would all invite heavy vehicles onto the bridge, which defeats the purpose of declaring anything about it. Matches option B.
context: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

subject: English

stem: The speech was so ____ that the audience applauded repeatedly.

stem: Identify the option that defines the homonyms 'gate' and 'gait' most appropriately.
optA: Gate means to achieve or receive, and gait means a person's manner of walking
optB: Gate means a hinged barrier used to close an opening in a wall, fence or hedge, and gait means a person's manner of walking
optC: Gate means general agreement on tariff and excise, and gait means a person's manner of talking
optD: Gate means a hinged barrier used to close an opening in a wall or fence, and gait means a cloth or leather leg covering reaching from the instep to above the ankle or to the mid-calf or knee
subject: English
solution: A gate is a hinged barrier that closes an opening in a wall, fence or hedge; a gait is a person's manner of walking. The two sound alike but are unrelated in sense, which is what makes them a homonym pair. The alternative that defines gait as a leg covering has confused it with 'gaiter'; the one glossing gate as 'to achieve or receive' has reached for 'get'; and the one offering 'general agreement on tariff and excise' has reached for the trade acronym and also misreports gait as a manner of talking. Matches option B.

stem:

Accept
subject: English
solution: A homonym here means a word that sounds the same but differs in meaning and spelling. 'Accept' means to receive or agree to something; 'except' means leaving out or apart from, and in ordinary speech the two are pronounced almost identically. Accent, expect and expert each differ in their vowels or consonants and are not sound-alikes for accept. Matches option C.

solution: Flair is a natural talent or a distinctive stylishness, which is what would set one chef's creations apart from ordinary restaurant fare. Flare is a sudden burst of flame or light, fair concerns justice or an event, and 'flere' is not an English word at all. Matches option D.

solution: To cast off is the phrasal verb for discarding something, and its past form is unchanged, which is what the parallel with 'and bought' requires. stem: The minimum age for the worker, to be employed in a factory, was fixed through first Factory Act, 1881. What was the minimum age?
subject: History
solution: The Factory Act of 1881, the first factory legislation in British India, prohibited the employment of children below the age of seven and restricted children between seven and twelve to nine hours of work a day. The figure nine is the daily hours limit rather than the minimum age, and that is exactly the confusion the question is built on. Matches option C.

stem: Who was the mastermind of Ryotwari system in India?
subject: History
subtopic: British Economic Policy and Industrial India
solution: Under the Ryotwari settlement revenue was fixed directly with the individual cultivator, or ryot, rather than through an intermediary zamindar. It was devised by Thomas Munro, working with Alexander Read, and introduced first in the Baramahal and then across the Madras Presidency. John Shore is associated with the Permanent Settlement of Bengal instead, and neither of the remaining administrators is linked to this system. Matches option A.

stem: In the process of reunification of the Extremists and the Liberals, who was the major architect?

solution: The reunion of Extremists and Moderates at the Lucknow session of 1916 was engineered chiefly by Annie Besant (with Tilak). stem: The second session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by
subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
solution: The second session of the Indian National Congress, held at Calcutta in 1886, was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who went on to preside over the Congress twice more. The first session at Bombay in 1885 had been presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee. Matches option C.

stem: In which of the following Sessions of the Indian National Congress Bal Gangadhar Tilak had expressed,"Swaraj is my birthright, I shall have it."
subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
solution: Tilak made the declaration during the Home Rule agitation, at the Lucknow session of 1916 - the same session that reunited the Moderates and the Extremists after nine years apart. The Surat session of 1907 is the tempting pick because it is the session most associated with Tilak, but it is remembered for the split rather than for the slogan. Matches option D.

stem: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Unrest'?
subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
solution: Valentine Chirol, in his book 'Indian Unrest', described Bal Gangadhar Tilak as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'. Tilak sued him for libel in London and lost the case. The name is printed here as 'Valentine Shirol'. Matches option C.

stem: Rabindranath Tagore got Knighthood in the year?
subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
solution: Rabindranath Tagore was knighted in 1915, two years after he received the Nobel Prize in Literature, and renounced the honour in 1919 in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Matches option B.

stem:

Information and broadcasting ,Government of India?

subject: History
subtopic: Freedom Movement — INC, Gandhi and Independence
solution: 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' was written by Surendra Nath Sen at the request of the Government of India for the centenary of the revolt and published by the Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, which makes it the official history. 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857' is Ramesh Chandra Majumdar's independent study, written outside the official commission and reaching notably different conclusions about the character of the revolt. stem: Who founded the Vijayanagara kingdom?
subject: History
solution: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 by the brothers Harihara and Bukka, sons of Sangama, and their line is therefore known as the Sangama dynasty. The Saluva and Tuluva lines ruled later in the empire's history, and Devaraya is the name borne by rulers within the Sangama line rather than a separate dynasty at all. Matches option B.

stem: Which book was written by Krishnadeva Raya?
subject: History
solution: Krishnadeva Raya, the Vijayanagara ruler who reigned from 1509 to 1529, wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu, a work on kingship and statecraft framed as the story of the saint Andal. Mitakshara is Vijnaneshwara's commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, Rajatarangini is Kalhana's chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, and Karpoor Manjari is Rajashekhara's Prakrit play. stem: Language used in Ashokan inscription is :
subject: History
solution: Ashoka's edicts were composed in Prakrit, the everyday spoken language of the time, and cut in Brahmi across most of the subcontinent and in Kharoshthi in the north-west; only the far north-western edicts add Greek and Aramaic. Sanskrit does not appear in royal inscriptions until Rudradaman's Junagadh record of the second century CE, Apabhramsa is a later stage of the language, and Hindi did not yet exist. Matches option B.

stem:

subject: History
solution: James Prinsep, an officer of the East India Company's Calcutta mint, worked out the Brahmi script in 1837 and so made Ashoka's edicts readable for the first time. Charles Wilkins and William Jones were earlier Orientalists whose work was on Sanskrit texts rather than on Brahmi. Matches option A.

stem: Which one of the following statements about Chandragupta II is not correct
optA: Kalidas and Amarsingh were famous scholars in his court
optB: He expanded his empire both through matrimonial alliances and conquests
optC: He married a Naga princess, named Kubera Naga
optD: He married his daughter Prabhawati to an Ahom prince
subject: History
solution: Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavati Gupta to Rudrasena II, a Vakataka prince of the Deccan, not to an Ahom prince; the Ahoms only entered Assam in the thirteenth century, some eight hundred years later. The other three statements hold: Kalidasa and Amarasimha are counted among the gems of his court, he expanded by conquest and by marriage alliance together, and he did marry the Naga princess Kuberanaga. Matches option D.

stem: What was government land called during the Maurya period?
subject: History
solution: Crown land cultivated directly by the Mauryan state was called sita, and the grain raised on it was the sita revenue. The Arthashastra names the officer who managed it, the Sitadhyaksha, which is the strongest evidence that the term is the state's own. Matches option B.

solution: AGMARK is the quality certification mark issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act of 1937 and stamped on graded farm goods such as ghee, honey, spices and edible oils. stem: Which of the following is the highest peak in South India?
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
solution: Anamudi, in the Anaimalai hills of Kerala, rises to about 2,695 m and is the highest point in India south of the Himalayas. Doddabetta in the Nilgiris reaches about 2,637 m and is the tempting near-miss; Amarkantak is a plateau in Madhya Pradesh and Mahendragiri is far lower. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following rivers of India crosses the tropic of cancer twice?
subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
solution: The Mahi rises in Madhya Pradesh, flows north into Rajasthan, then swings west and south-west through Gujarat to the Gulf of Khambhat. That hairpin course carries it over the Tropic of Cancer once on the way north and again on the way back south, which no other Indian river does. The Chambal stays north of the Tropic throughout and the Narmada runs well to the south of it, so neither crosses it even once. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
optA: Geologically Peninsular region is India’s most ancient part
optB: Himalaya mountains demonstrate the most newly developed folded mountains in the world
optC: The Western coastline of India is formed by the deposition process of the rivers
optD: Gondwana rocks have the largest reserve of coal in India
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
solution: India's western coastline is narrow and largely erosional, because the short, swift west-flowing rivers such as the Narmada and the Tapi reach the sea through estuaries and build no deltas. It is the eastern coastline that is built by river deposition, carrying the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri deltas. The other three statements are correct as they stand. Matches option C.

stem: Which one of the following coasts of India is located between Krishna delta and Cape Comorin?
subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
solution: The east coast is divided into two named stretches: the Northern Circars, running from the Mahanadi delta to the Krishna delta, and the Coromandel Coast, running from the Krishna delta south to Cape Comorin. Malabar and Konkan are stretches of the west coast and can be set aside at once. Matches option A.

stem: The only landlocked Country in Southeast Asia is-
subject: Geography
solution: Laos has no sea frontier at all, being enclosed by China, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand and Myanmar. Every other state of Southeast Asia, mainland or island, reaches the sea. Matches option B.

stem: Which Strait separates Europe from Africa :
subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
solution: The Strait of Gibraltar, about 14 km wide at its narrowest, divides Spain from Morocco and so separates Europe from Africa while joining the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The Bosphorus separates Europe from Asia, Dover separates Britain from France, and Bering separates Asia from North America. Matches option B.

stem: The Tornadoes are very strong tropical cyclones originating in:
subject: Geography
solution: In the naming scheme used for violent tropical storms, the Caribbean and the neighbouring Atlantic form the source region on that side of the world, while the China Sea is the home of typhoons and the Arabian Sea produces ordinary cyclones. The Black Sea is small and enclosed and produces none. Only the Caribbean therefore fits. It is worth knowing that a tornado is strictly not a tropical cyclone at all but a small, short-lived funnel of violently rotating air, most frequent over the plains of the United States. Matches option A.

stem: The world’s largest and most dense forests are in-
subject: Geography
solution: Brazil holds the greater part of the Amazon basin, the largest and densest continuous block of tropical rainforest on earth, covering roughly 5.5 million square kilometres. Canada's boreal forest is vast in area but far thinner in canopy and species, and neither India nor Tanzania is in the same class. Matches option C.

stem: Blue Green Algae is used as biofertilizer to induce which of the following crop productions?
subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Agriculture, Crops, Soils and Land Use
solution: Blue-green algae such as Anabaena and Nostoc fix atmospheric nitrogen and need standing water to thrive, which is exactly the condition of a flooded paddy field. They are therefore used as a biofertiliser for rice. Wheat, gram and mustard are grown on dry fields where these algae cannot establish themselves. Matches option B.

stem: Valley of the King is located in –
subject: Geography
solution: The Valley of the Kings lies on the west bank of the Nile opposite Luxor in Egypt and holds the rock-cut tombs of the New Kingdom pharaohs, Tutankhamun's among them. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following region is famous for ‘Lapps’ tribe?
subject: Geography
solution: The Lapps, who call themselves the Sami, are the reindeer-herding people of the Arctic fringe of Scandinavia, spread across northern Norway, Sweden and Finland and into the Kola peninsula. The Inuit occupy Alaska and Greenland, which is where the other choices point. Matches option B.

stem: The Asteroids are small celestial bodies in the solar system which are found between the planets.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth in Space, Maps and Coordinates
solution: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, where Jupiter's gravity kept the fragments stirred up so that they never gathered into a planet. Matches option B.

stem: The famous Volcanic mountain 'Karakatoa' is situated in which of the following countries?
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
solution: Krakatoa is a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra in Indonesia. Its eruption of 1883 was among the most violent in recorded history and was heard thousands of kilometres away. Matches option B.

stem: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees Indian citizens:
optD: Equality before law and equal protection of the laws
subject: Polity
chapter: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Local Governance
solution: Article 14 reads that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. It therefore carries two guarantees, not one: equality before the law, the British idea that nobody stands above the ordinary law, and equal protection of the laws, the American idea that those in like circumstances be treated alike. Choosing only one of the pair is the trap the question sets. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following is opposite to the principle of “Rule of Law”?
subject: Polity
chapter: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Local Governance
solution: Rule of law, as Dicey set it out, rests on the supremacy of ordinary law and on equality before it, so that no person or class sits outside the reach of the courts. Special privileges and immunities put some people beyond that ordinary law and are its direct contradiction. Equality before law and equal opportunity are expressions of the rule of law rather than opposites of it. Matches option B.

stem: Which discrimination of the various grounds below, by the State is not prohibited in Article– 15 of the Constitution?
subject: Polity
chapter: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Local Governance
solution: Article 15 forbids the State from discriminating against a citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Language does not appear in that list; linguistic protection is dealt with separately, chiefly under Articles 29 and 30. Matches option C.

stem: The Articles – 17 and 18 of constitution provide.
subject: Polity
chapter: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Local Governance
solution: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and Article 18 abolishes titles. Both strike at inherited rank and stigma rather than at wealth, votes or worship, so together they secure social equality. Matches option A.

stem: Right to Privacy comes under
subject: Polity
chapter: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Local Governance
solution: In K. S. Puttaswamy versus Union of India, decided in 2017, a nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court held privacy to be a fundamental right flowing from the right to life and personal liberty guaranteed by Article 21. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following statement is not correct about 'Bombay Plan'?
optA: The Bombay Plan is also called the 'Tata Bidla Plan'
optC: Its draft was prepared by the John Mathai
optD: There were 10 members in this plan
subject: Economics
subtopic: Five Year Plans and Indian Planning
solution: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was drawn up and signed by eight industrialists, not ten, so the claim about its membership is the false one. The rest hold: it is popularly called the Tata-Birla Plan, it did appear in 1944, and John Mathai, later independent India's finance minister, was among the authors who prepared the draft. Matches option D.

stem: The ratio of the focal length of the objective to the focal length of the eyepiece is greater than one for
subject: Physics
solution: In a refracting telescope the objective has a long focal length and the eyepiece a short one, so \(\frac{f_{o}}{f_{e}}\) is greater than one and that ratio is the magnifying power itself. The compound microscope is built the other way round: its objective focal length is only a few millimetres while the eyepiece runs to several centimetres, so the same ratio is less than one. Matches option B.

stem: Cyclotron is a device used to ______.
subject: Physics
solution: The cyclotron uses a steady magnetic field to bend charged particles into a spiral and an alternating electric field across the dees to give them a push twice every revolution, so their speed and energy climb steadily. It is built for heavy positive ions such as protons, deuterons and alpha particles; electrons gain relativistic mass so quickly that they fall out of step with the alternating field. Matches option B.

A wire has a resistance of 32 Ω. It is melted and drawn into a wire of half of its original length. What is the resistance
of the new wire?
subject: Physics
solution: Melting and redrawing conserves volume, so halving the length doubles the area. \(R' = \rho(L/2)/(2A) = R/4 = 32/4 = 8\ \Omega\).

stem: The most suitable metal for making permanent magnets is:
subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
solution: Permanent magnets need high retentivity, so the material keeps its magnetism once the field is removed, and high coercivity, so a stray field cannot wipe it out. Steel has both. Soft iron magnetises very strongly but loses it the instant the current stops, which is exactly what an electromagnet wants and a permanent magnet does not, while copper and aluminium are not ferromagnetic at all. Matches option B.

stem: The depth \(d\) at which the value of acceleration due to gravity becomes \(\frac{1}{n}\) times the value at the surface, is [\(R\) = radius of the earth]
subject: Physics
solution: Inside the earth the acceleration due to gravity falls linearly with depth, \(g_{d} = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)\). Setting \(g_{d} = \frac{g}{n}\) gives \(1 - \frac{d}{R} = \frac{1}{n}\), so \(\frac{d}{R} = \frac{n-1}{n}\) and \(d = R\left(\frac{n-1}{n}\right)\). The tempting choices assume an inverse-square fall, which is how \(g\) behaves with height but not with depth. Matches option B.

stem: An object is placed at 20 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 10 cm. The image formed by the mirror is
optA: Real and at 20 cm from the mirror
optB: Virtual and at 20 cm from the mirror
optC: Virtual and at 20/3 cm from the mirror
optD: Real and at 20/3 cm from the mirror
subject: Physics
solution: Apply \(\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\) with \(u = -20\) cm and, for a convex mirror, \(f = +10\) cm. Then \(\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{3}{20}\), giving \(v = \frac{20}{3}\) cm. The positive sign places the image behind the mirror, so it is virtual, erect and diminished. Since a convex mirror can never form a real image of a real object, both real choices can be discarded before any arithmetic is done. Matches option C.

stem: The temperature of a place on one sunny day is 113 in Fahrenheit scale. The Kelvin scale reading of this temperature will be
subject: Physics
solution: Convert F to C: \(C = \frac{5}{9}(F-32) = \frac{5}{9}(113-32) = \frac{5}{9} \times 81 = 45°\text{C}\). Convert to Kelvin: \(K = 45 + 273 = 318\) K. Matches option A: 318 K.

stem: The displacement-time graph of a particle acted upon by a constant force is
optD: any curve depending upon initial conditions
subject: Physics
solution: Constant force means constant acceleration, and with constant acceleration the displacement follows \(s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\). Displacement is quadratic in time, so the graph is a parabola; a straight line would require zero acceleration and therefore zero force. The suggestion that the shape depends on the initial conditions is tempting, but a different starting velocity only shifts and tilts the same curve, and the quadratic term set by the acceleration is always present. Matches option C.

stem: To convert galvanometer into voltmeter one should connect:
optA: high resistance in series with galvanometer
optB: low resistance in series with galvanometer
optC: high resistance in parallel with galvanometer
optD: low resistance in parallel with galvanometer
subject: Physics
solution: The galvanometer coil takes only a very small current, so to read a potential difference it must be given a large resistance in series, which drops nearly all the applied voltage and lets only a tiny current through the coil. That series resistance also raises the total resistance of the instrument, which is what an ideal voltmeter needs so it does not disturb the circuit it is measuring. Putting a small resistance in parallel instead gives the shunt used to make an ammeter, which is the standard confusion here. Matches option A.

stem: A current loop placed in a non-uniform magnetic field experiences
subject: Physics
solution: In a uniform field the forces on opposite sides of the loop are equal and opposite, so they cancel and only a turning effect survives; that is why a motor coil rotates without drifting. If the field is non-uniform the forces on the two sides are no longer equal, so a net force appears as well, while the torque is still there in general. Whether that net force pulls or pushes depends on how the loop is oriented, so neither attraction nor repulsion can be named on its own. Matches option D.

stem: Water is usually heated by
subject: Physics
solution: Water is a poor conductor of heat, so heating a vessel from below works by convection: the warmed layer at the bottom expands, becomes less dense and rises, cooler water sinks to take its place, and the circulating current carries heat through the whole body of liquid. Conduction alone would leave the top cold, and radiation plays almost no part at these temperatures. Matches option B.

stem: ‘Mirage’ is a phenomenon due to
subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
solution: On a hot road the air just above the surface is much hotter, and so optically rarer, than the air above it. Light from the sky travelling downwards bends further and further away from the normal as it crosses these layers, and once its angle of incidence passes the critical angle it is turned back upwards altogether, so the observer sees a patch of sky lying on the road and reads it as water. Refraction is the tempting choice because it is what bends the ray in the first place, but the ray is only returned to the eye by total internal reflection, and offering both in the same list is precisely what makes that the discriminator. Matches option C.

stem: The top of Lake is frozen as the atmospheric temperature is \(-10^{\circ}\text{C}\). The temperature at the bottom of the lake is most likely to be
subject: Physics
solution: Water is densest at \(4^{\circ}\text{C}\). As a lake loses heat, water chilled to that temperature sinks and gathers at the bottom; cooling it further makes it lighter again, so the colder water stays on top and eventually freezes there. The bottom therefore settles at about \(4^{\circ}\text{C}\) and the fish survive under the ice, whatever the air above the surface is doing. Matches option C.

Assertion : The value of acceleration due to gravity does not depend upon mass of the body on which force is applied.
Reason : Acceleration due to gravity is a constant quantity.
optA: Assertion is true & Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
optB: Assertion is true & Reason is not correct explanation of Assertion
optC: Assertion is true & Reason is false
optD: Assertion is false & Reason is true
subject: Physics
solution: The assertion is true. Since \(g = \frac{GM}{r^{2}}\), it is fixed by the mass of the earth and the distance from its centre, and the mass of the falling body cancels out, which is why a stone and a feather fall together in a vacuum. The reason is false, because \(g\) is not a constant at all: it falls with height, it falls with depth, and it is larger at the poles than at the equator. stem: An electric fuse works on the:
subject: Physics
solution: The fuse is a short length of wire with high resistivity and a low melting point, placed in series with the circuit it protects. When the current rises past the rated value the heat produced, \(H = I^{2}Rt\), melts that wire and breaks the circuit, so the fuse depends squarely on the heating effect of current. The magnetic effect is what a miniature circuit breaker or a relay uses instead, which is the tempting alternative here, and neither chemical action nor light plays any part. Matches option D.

stem:
Consider the following statements
1. Pulmonary artery is the only vein in which the impure blood is circulated from heart to lungs.
2. Pulmonary vein is the only artery in which the pure blood is circulated from lungs to heart.
3. Deoxygenated blood is circulated in the arteries.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
subject: Biology
solution: The first two statements describe the right vessels doing the right jobs. Blood low in oxygen leaves the heart for the lungs through the pulmonary artery, and oxygen-rich blood returns from the lungs to the heart through the pulmonary vein, and those two are the standing exceptions to the usual pattern. The third statement is wrong, because arteries as a class carry oxygenated blood, and only the pulmonary artery, together with the umbilical artery in a foetus, carries the deoxygenated kind. Note the loose wording of the first two, which call the pulmonary artery a vein and the pulmonary vein an artery: a vessel is named by whether it leads away from or towards the heart, never by the kind of blood inside it. Matches option C.
reviewNote: KEY CORRECTED from the printed (a) to (c). Statements 1 and 2 are exactly symmetric -- the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart, the pulmonary vein oxygenated blood to it. If 1 is accepted, 2 must be. Statement 3 is false.

stem: The difference between a nuclear reactor and atomic bomb is that
optA: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor while in the atomic bomb there is a chain reaction
optB: the chain reacation in nuclear reactor is controlled
optC: the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
optD: no chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb while it takes place in nuclear reactor
subject: Physics
solution: Both a reactor and a bomb run on the same fission chain reaction, so any statement denying a chain reaction in one of them is wrong at once. The real difference is control: in a reactor, rods of cadmium or boron absorb the surplus neutrons so that on average exactly one neutron from each fission goes on to cause the next, and the output stays steady. stem: Which one among the following statements regarding the properties of mixtures and compounds is not correct?

optC: The constituents of a mixture can be separated by physical methods but those of a compound cannot be separated by physical methods
optD: Energy is either absorbed or evolved during the preparation of a mixture but not in the preparation of a compound
subject: Chemistry
solution: The statement about energy has the two cases the wrong way round. Making a compound breaks old bonds and forms new ones, so heat is absorbed or given out; making a mixture merely places substances side by side, so there is normally no appreciable energy change. The other three statements are standard and correct: a mixture keeps the properties of its constituents while a compound has entirely new ones, a mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous while a compound is always homogeneous, and a mixture can be separated by physical means while a compound cannot. Matches option D.

stem: What happened when a hard boiled egg after shelling is immersed in saturated brine?
optD: It initially grows in size and then shrinks
subject: Biology
solution: Saturated brine is strongly hypertonic to the egg, so water moves out of the egg's protein gel across its membrane by osmosis, travelling down the water-potential gradient from the egg into the salt solution. Losing water, the egg shrinks and its surface wrinkles. It would swell only in the opposite case, if it were put into pure water or another hypotonic solution, so there is no stage at which it first grows. Matches option A.
reviewNote: KEY CORRECTED from the printed (c) to (a). Saturated brine is hypertonic to the egg, so water leaves it by osmosis and the egg shrinks. OPTION TEXT CORRECTED: Option (d) is printed truncated at 'and then'.
